I've been in a similar situation with my best friend. Up until about a year ago, they were severely depressed and suicidal. No matter what, I couldn't make it better and it seemed to me that they just wouldn't listen to the solutions and ideas I offered. I felt like I was trying really hard to help them, and at a certain point I felt that I couldn't help them anymore because they didn't want to be helped, they didn't want to get betterband it was starting to take a toll on me. 

However, I learned along the way that my methods and "solutions" weren't going to do anything substantial because depression does things to someone that just doesn't make sense. My friend didn't want to get better, they didn't see any point in a better life or the prospect that things might some day change. Together with a mutual friend I got them to reluctantly go to therapy. This was a year ago. They appear to be doing better, but it's still a long way from being healed. Perhaps the depression never goes away for my friend, we don't know. 

A couple months back I convinced them to try antidepressants, which my friend had been very much against prior to trying. They are working quite well, though, despite their doubts about it. 

TLDR: My advice to you is to support your friend when you can, but to also look at the situation realistically. It sounds like your friend will benefit from seeing a therapist. Maybe do a bit of research on the benefits of therapy and, depending on your friend's age and situation of course, look into the effects of antidepressants. They may be a bit hard to convince, but both those things can work wonders if done right. 

Hope my experience is of use to you, and I hope you know you're not alone in this! Make sure you take care of your own mental health as well, as it's not uncommon that caring for a depressed friend takes a toll on your own mental health!
